title: 63 Tonnes of Bronze: China's Heaviest Ancient Bell | China Travel Expert
description:
Inside Beijing's Bell Tower hangs the heaviest surviving ancient bell in China - about 63 tonnes of cast bronze.

The bronze bell is roughly 7.02 m tall and 3.4 m across, and for centuries it was Beijing's official timekeeper, struck at dusk and dawn to open and close the city gates. It fell silent in 1924, when the Bell Tower stopped keeping the capital's time.

Then, on New Year's Eve 1990 - after 66 years of silence - the great bell was struck again to ring in the new year, and it has marked the turning of the year since.

🧭 Expert Tip: climb the steep stone staircase inside the Bell Tower to stand right next to the bell, then walk 100 m south to the Drum Tower - the two were a single timekeeping pair, and the view between them is one of old Beijing's best.

北京钟楼内的青铜大钟重约 63 吨、高约 7.02 米，是中国现存最重的古钟；1924 年停敲，1990 年除夕时隔 66 年后重新敲响。
